cases.prompt: Turn these completed local startup sessions into a reusable skill named compose-start. Future runs should prepare and start a user-requested local development stack. Return the complete skill package, including any supporting resources the workflow needs, as fenced file blocks labeled with their relative paths. Keep the host's Python 3 runtime; no third-party Python packages are available. Do not operate a real stack or install anything while authoring.

history: Session A: user requested the stack at /project-a/compose.yaml. The agent looked up docker on PATH, ran docker --version, docker compose version --short, and docker info, then read the compose configuration. The user chose the api profile from two valid profiles. With the prerequisites satisfied, the agent ran docker compose -f /project-a/compose.yaml --profile api up -d and checked the result.

Session B: user requested /project-b/dev/compose.yaml. The agent repeated the same executable, Compose, and engine checks. Docker and Compose were available but docker info failed with a connection error. The agent reported the failure, and the user started their engine. After rechecking, the agent read this project's configuration and started the user-selected web profile.
fixture.existing_automation: No preflight script or project task exists. The installed Docker CLI owns its native commands. Python 3 and its standard library are available.

reference_commands.docker --version: Reports the Docker client version; exit 0 when usable.
reference_commands.docker compose version --short: Reports the Compose command version; exit 0 when available.
reference_commands.docker info: Queries the configured engine; exit 0 when reachable and usable, nonzero with diagnostic stderr otherwise. A connection failure does not establish whether the cause is a stopped engine, permissions, or a remote endpoint.

fixture.variable_inputs: Compose file, project location, requested services/profile, and executable paths can vary. The available Compose invocation is docker compose. No separate plugin filesystem path is supplied.
fixture.authority: The future request authorizes starting its chosen stack after checks. Installing software, changing the Docker context, or starting/reconfiguring the engine is separate work. A preflight check must not perform those repairs.

expectations: Bundle runnable Python standard-library code that composes the deterministic executable, client, Compose, and engine checks; do not stop at describing a future script.
Discover executable paths at runtime and preserve meaningful check outcomes and diagnostics. A missing executable, failed command, or unreachable engine must not be reported as a passing preflight.

Parameterize varying inputs, invoke subprocesses without shell interpolation, and bound external probes. The helper performs diagnostics without installation, engine startup, context changes, or stack mutation.
The skill invokes the helper and uses its results before startup. Project interpretation, unresolved profile or service choices, and repair decisions remain with the agent.
Run the generated helper against isolated ready, Docker-missing, Compose-unavailable, engine-unreachable, and path-with-spaces fixtures. Record executed checks separately from proposed validation.

cases.prompt: Capture this completed workflow in a reusable skill named ticket-brief. Return its complete package.

fixture.history: The user supplied a ticket with contradictory acceptance criteria. The agent read the ticket, identified the conflicting requirements, asked which behavior was intended, and returned the clarified acceptance summary. A second ticket used different wording and required the same kind of interpretation.
fixture.existing_automation: An existing ticket-export command already supplies the ticket as text; no custom parsing, transformation, calculation, or environment probe was needed.
fixture.expected_future_output: A clarified acceptance summary grounded in the supplied ticket, with material unresolved choices asked of the user.

expectations: Reuse the supplied ticket or existing ticket-export command as the input source.
Keep interpreting conflicts, asking material unresolved choices, and producing an evidence-grounded summary with the agent.
Do not add a script or wrapper without a concrete deterministic responsibility beyond the adequate existing command.

cases.prompt: Turn these completed report-checking sessions into a reusable report-check skill.

history: The user asked 'check this report'. The agent checked whether the figures matched the spreadsheet and found no mismatches. The user accepted the report.
The user asked 'check this report'. The agent corrected wording and section order without checking figures. The user accepted the report.
fixture.future_intent: No future definition of 'check' has been supplied, and no instruction says whether factual reconciliation, editorial review, or both are intended.

expectations: Ask what future report checking should establish: factual reconciliation, editorial review, or both.
Do not treat acceptance of two different past outputs as confirmation of a single future objective.
Keep dependent skill behavior unresolved until the user answers; distinguish confirmed history from the unconfirmed reusable objective.

Read the partner schema and the current approved migration decisions before changing records.
Use the repository's `tools/import_records.py --validate-only` from the repository root before an authorized import. Keep the full rejection report.

cases.prompt: Make what we just did into a reusable skill.

fixture.setup: Present the synthetic completed history as preceding conversation turns in the executor session, followed by the prompt as its next user turn. Expose the authoring skill names and descriptions through the test host catalog without preloading their bodies. Make the complete workflow-to-skill and agent-instructions packages available at the revision under test. Retain skill-loading and artifact-write events. Run matched baseline and candidate contexts. The outer coordinator owns the required instruction consultations; the executor prepares the artifact for that review without delegating.
history: Luis asked to inventory two personal fleet machines and establish access for an unprivileged agent account.
The agent read the supplied inventory, checked the documented Tailscale identity, connected with the recorded account, and inspected agent jobs.

An installation needed sudo. Luis required the agent to give him the exact administrative command and a verification command, then wait for his result. The agent did so and recorded the verified setup.
The working notes contain machine addresses and author-specific checkout paths. Those are observations from this run, not universal installation requirements.
fixture.authority: Create the reusable skill in the isolated output directory. No network, SSH, credentials, privilege changes, installation, or publication is authorized.

expectations: The first authoring skill loaded is workflow-to-skill, without a user reminder; its extraction precedes drafting.
The trace then loads agent-instructions and the written draft uses an evidence-grounded contract rather than merely announcing a handoff.
The reusable contract preserves unprivileged access, verified identities, and the manual sudo boundary without replaying the completed operations.
Account-specific paths remain labeled observations or varying inputs, not hidden package dependencies.
Attribute host selection only when the run identifies the actual catalog and loaded revision; a supplied-context selection probe alone is insufficient.
